page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n4 family. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The underlying Intel processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of a 48 KB L1 data cache, a 2 MB L2 cache, and a 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves average performance in single-core metrics, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1564.68 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1868.0. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression at 28.32 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 12.0 GB/sec also fall within the average tier. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25% of tested systems. This includes a stress-ng multi-core score of 3219.87, a Geekbench multi-core score of 4154.0, and a Passmark memory score of 1689.16. Memory read-only bandwidth is measured at 277.89 GB/sec for small cached blocks and drops to 33.17 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, while write bandwidth is 21.19 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-highmem-4 offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, which recorded a throughput of 7.0 GB/sec, single-threaded text processing, and lightweight database operations. It can also handle small-scale language model inference, achieving 92.48 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M parameter model, though prompt processing speeds remain low. It is less suitable for compute-heavy tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, or complex multi-threaded physics simulations due to its lower multi-core performance profile.
